block.swordsmith.forge.hint: Feed it charcoal, light it with flint and steel, pump the bellows for heat. Right-click with stock to heat it
block.swordsmith.smithing_anvil.hint: Lay hot stock on it and strike with the hammer. Final hilt assembly happens here too
block.swordsmith.quenching_barrel.hint: Fill with a water bucket, then plunge a cherry-red blade (780-950°C) to harden it
block.swordsmith.whetstone.hint: Right-click with a tempered blade to grind its edge (while cold)
item.swordsmith.iron_bloom.hint: Spongy smelted iron. Heat it past 720°C and hammer the slag out on the anvil
item.swordsmith.steel_billet.hint: Consolidated steel. Heat it again and draw it out into a bar
item.swordsmith.blade_preform.hint: A drawn-out bar. Keep forging to set the point, bevels and tang
item.swordsmith.rough_blade.hint: Blade-shaped at last. Heat to cherry red (780-950°C) and plunge it into the quenching barrel. Overheat it and it will crack
item.swordsmith.cracked_blade.hint: Quenched too hot and cracked... Reheat and forge it back into a rough blade
item.swordsmith.quenched_blade.hint: Glass-hard but brittle. Temper it in a lit forge without bellows blast (~300°C) — above 460°C the hardness is lost
item.swordsmith.tempered_blade.hint: Hard yet springy. Grind it on the sharpening wheel once it is cold
item.swordsmith.sharp_blade.hint: A finished blade with a real edge. Lay it on the anvil and fit guard, grip, then pommel
item.swordsmith.sword_guard.hint: Protects the hand. The first piece fitted onto a sharpened blade
item.swordsmith.sword_grip.hint: A leather-wrapped wooden grip. Fitted after the guard
item.swordsmith.sword_pommel.hint: The counterweight. Fitted last, then peened tight with the hammer
item.swordsmith.smithing_hammer.hint: Right-click hot metal on the anvil to forge it
item.swordsmith.smithing_tongs.hint: Hold these in either hand to handle hot metal without burns (they wear out instead)
item.swordsmith.bellows.hint: Blast air into a lit forge, pushing the fire toward 1280°C
item.swordsmith.forged_steel_sword.hint: Born of fire, anvil, water and stone — the only one of its kind
msg.swordsmith.too_hot_to_hold: It burns! You need smithing tongs in hand to hold this
msg.swordsmith.fuel_full: The forge is already full of fuel
msg.swordsmith.need_fuel: No fuel. Add charcoal or coal
msg.swordsmith.need_lit: The forge is not lit. Use flint and steel
msg.swordsmith.forge_occupied: Something is already heating in the forge
msg.swordsmith.anvil_empty: Nothing on the anvil. Right-click with hot stock to lay it down
msg.swordsmith.not_forgeable: That is not something to forge here
msg.swordsmith.too_cold: The metal is too cold to move. Bring it back to 720°C+ in the forge
msg.swordsmith.need_sharp_blade: Fit parts onto a sharpened blade lying on the anvil
msg.swordsmith.attach_hot: The blade is still hot — let it cool before assembly
msg.swordsmith.attach_need_guard: Slide the guard onto the blade first
msg.swordsmith.attach_need_pommel: Finally, cap it with the pommel
msg.swordsmith.peen_hint: Peen the pommel tight with your hammer
msg.swordsmith.sword_finished: The sword is finished! Right-click bare-handed to take it
msg.swordsmith.barrel_empty: The barrel is dry. Fill it with a water bucket
msg.swordsmith.quench_ok: Hsssss! A clean quench — the edge is hard
msg.swordsmith.quench_crack: Crack... it went in too hot and the shock split the blade
msg.swordsmith.quench_weak: Too cool — no hardness took (quench from 780-950°C)
msg.swordsmith.quench_cold: The blade is cold. Heat it to 780-950°C before quenching
msg.swordsmith.grind_already_sharp: This blade is already sharp. Assemble the hilt on the anvil
msg.swordsmith.barrel_full: The barrel is already full of water
msg.swordsmith.grind_hot: Too hot to grind — you would ruin the temper. Let it cool
msg.swordsmith.grind_wrong: This blade is not ready for grinding. Forge, quench and temper it first
